prompt: /deep-research Of the mosses listed by Putzke in 2015 as having been collected in at least 3 of the 4 given locations (King George Island, Elephant Island, Nelson Island and Hope Bay), which species are also found in South Australia? Refer to Catcheside's 1980 list and compare the names as they appear in these sources, ignoring any potential name changes.
instruction: Of the mosses listed by Putzke in 2015 as having been collected in at least 3 of the 4 given locations (King George Island, Elephant Island, Nelson Island and Hope Bay), which species are also found in South Australia? Refer to Catcheside's 1980 list and compare the names as they appear in these sources, ignoring any potential name changes.
answer:
Now I have both complete datasets. Let me analyze them systematically.

**From Putzke et al. 2015 (Table 1):** 46 species across 4 locations. Species found in **at least 3 of 4 locations** (King George Island, Elephant Island, Nelson Island, Hope Bay):

1. Sanionia uncinata (4)
2. Andreaea depressinervis (4)
3. Andreaea gainii (4)
4. Andreaea regularis (4)
5. Bryum argenteum (3 - KG, EI, NI)
6. Bryum orbiculatifolium (3 - KG, EI, HB)
7. Bryum pseudotriquetrum (3 - KG, EI, HB)
8. Pohlia nutas (3 - KG, EI, NI)
9. Pohlia wahlenbergii (3 - KG, EI, NI)
10. Ceratodon grossiretis (3 - KG, EI, HB)
11. Polytrichum alpinum (3 - KG, EI, HB)
12. Polytrichum juniperinum (3 - KG, EI, HB)
13. Hennediella antarctica (3 - KG, EI, NI)
14. Hennediella heimii (3 - KG, EI, NI)
15. Syntrichia saxicola (3 - KG, EI, NI)

**From Catcheside 1980 (Appendix):** Complete list of 184 South Australian moss species.

Cross-referencing the 15 Putzke species (≥3 locations) against the Catcheside 1980 South Australia list:

| Putzke 2015 species | In Catcheside 1980 SA? | Catcheside entry |
|---------------------|------------------------|------------------|
| Sanionia uncinata | No | — |
| Andreaea depressinervis | No | — |
| Andreaea gainii | No | — |
| Andreaea regularis | No | — |
| **Bryum argenteum** | **Yes** | "B. argenteum (A. I, w)" — bipolar group I(g) |
| Bryum orbiculatifolium | No | — |
| **Bryum pseudotriquetrum** | **Yes** | "B. pseudotriquetrum (q)" — bipolar group I(g) |
| Pohlia nutas | No | — |
| Pohlia wahlenbergii | No | — |
| Ceratodon grossiretis | No | (only *C. purpureus* listed) |
| Polytrichum alpinum | No | — |
| **Polytrichum juniperinum** | **Yes** | "Polytrichum juniperinum (1)" — bipolar group I(g) |
| Hennediella antarctica | No | — |
| Hennediella heimii | No | — |
| Syntrichia saxicola | No | (Syntrichia spp. not listed) |

---

**Answer:** Three species from Putzke's 2015 table (occurring in ≥3 of the 4 Antarctic locations) also appear in Catcheside's 1980 South Australia list, using the names exactly as printed in each source:

1. **Bryum argenteum** — Putzke: King George, Elephant, Nelson Islands; Catcheside: "B. argenteum (A. I, w)"
2. **Bryum pseudotriquetrum** — Putzke: King George, Elephant, Hope Bay; Catcheside: "B. pseudotriquetrum (q)"
3. **Polytrichum juniperinum** — Putzke: King George, Elephant, Hope Bay; Catcheside: "Polytrichum juniperinum (1)"

---

## Sources
- Putzke et al. 2015, *Revista Chilena de Historia Natural* 88:6, Table 1 — https://www.scielo.cl/pdf/rchnat/v88/06.pdf
- Catcheside 1982 (citing Catcheside 1980), *J. Hattori Bot. Lab.* 52:57–64, Appendix — https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/jhbl/52/0/52_57/_pdf
